Resolves #19990

A popup's tab strips now project the main window's drag contract. A tab dragged inside a popup shows the dock's previews and docks there. A tab dragged out of a popup tears out into a new vessel. The contract lives once, on the root (`VesselWorkspace#getDockDragContract`): the root keeps the tear-out machine and stays every vessel's opener, and each window supplies its own boundary, preview controller and identity. The root's tear-out seams follow the participant that owns the dragged item instead of assuming main, and a popup moves a vessel main opened through its opener's handle (`Neo.Main#windowMoveTo`).

Evidence: L3 (headless Chrome through the Neural Link fixture, the popup window's real pointer; all four arms red on `dev`) → L3 required (AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, AC-4).

| AC | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `WorkstationPopupTabDragNL.spec.mjs`, first arm, reads the popup's live sort zones mid-drag. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: the same arm parks Audit on the popup's right root edge. The popup's own preview reads `edge-right`, and the release splits the popup's stack with Audit on the right. Holds where the popup does not lie over main; see Deltas. |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: the second arm drags Audit out of the popup. The root admits a vessel, main opens it, the popup's moves reach its live handle, and the release transfers the same pane into `workstation-vessel:audit`. The third arm cancels such a drag and the pane comes home. The fourth tears out a popup's last tab and the emptied popup closes. Every tab except the popup's own; see Deltas. |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: `WorkstationStackReturnSplitNL.spec.mjs` drives the real ⠿ handle out of a popup into main (three arms, one a two-pane stack), and `DockTabSortZone.spec.mjs` pins the stack drag to the generic claim path. |
| AC-5 | CI-covered: the new spec runs in the hosted `e2e-brain` tier. |

## Deltas from ticket
- **Main opens every vessel**, including one for a tab leaving a popup. Per the ticket's trap (#19533), the vessel's handle and lifetime stay with the window that outlives every popup. The native close and `windowMoveTo` both resolve the handle in the opener. Under #19533's product condition (the site may open pop-ups), main needs no activation for this; without it the exit fails closed in-window, as any refused tear-out does.
- **A popup moves that vessel through its opener.** The drag runs in the popup, whose `Main` holds no handle for it, so `Main#windowMoveTo` now asks `window.opener` when it has no handle by that name.
- **The root's seams follow the item's owner** (`resolveItemWorkspaceId`):
  - the detach check runs on the popup's reducer;
  - the transfer's source is the popup;
  - a cancelled vessel restores the pane to the popup instead of promoting it;
  - the vessel opens at the proxy's position in the popup's frame;
  - a popup the tear-out empties retires before the vessel mounts, so a failed mount cannot leave it open.
- **One contract for both windows.** `getDockDragContract` replaces the root's inline option list. The popup had re-listed only part of it, which is how its strips became resort-only.
- **AC-4 needed an engine guard.** Arming vessel conversion on the popup's strip also handed its ⠿ drags to main as a converted tab-header proxy. Then the whole-stack return failed intermittently: 3 of 210 regression arms, all at the stack return, and 1 of 6 repeats of the stack-return spec. A whole-stack drag never rides a vessel, so `TabSortZone#resolveRemoteDragTransition` now keeps it on the generic path, as on `dev`. The ⠿ proxy no longer sticks at the popup's edge once the pointer leaves it, since `allowOverdrag` now arms the popup's strips.
- **AC-2 where the popup lies over main:** a drag at a popup point that main also covers is claimed by main and dropped there, on `dev` too. That is likely the report's "not always". Filed as #20004 with a fork on ADR 0029. The arms here aim where the windows do not overlap and assert that precondition.
- **AC-3's "every time" excludes the popup's own tab:** its derived vessel key is still bound to the popup, so the reservation refuses it. Filed as #20006.
- `Participation#resolveAffordances` is public: the popup's in-window seams use the controller its participation composes, so a popup paints one preview tier.
- Out of scope, noted in a defect-note: a tear-out released about 1.5 s after its vessel loads fails the vessel's mount ("left its pane in provisional chrome"), identically from main on `dev`.

## Test Evidence
- **On `dev`'s source all four arms are red:**
  - arm 1, because the popup's zone has `allowOverdrag: false`;
  - arm 2, because no vessel is admitted;
  - arms 3 and 4, because no vessel ever opens.
- **One mutation per defect; each turns only its own arm red:**
  - without the opener delegation: arm 2 at the live-handle check, plus the `MainWindowMoveTo` unit case;
  - without the owner-aware detach: arm 2 at the transfer (Audit stays in the popup);
  - with main as the transfer source: arm 2 at the transfer;
  - with main-only `sourceOwns`: arm 3 (the pane keeps the closed vessel's window);
  - with the retirement after the vessel mount: arm 4 (the popup stays open);
  - measuring the vessel against main's frame: the `Workspace.spec.mjs` placement case;
  - without the stack guard: its `DockTabSortZone.spec.mjs` case.
- **Stack return, `WorkstationStackReturnSplitNL` repeats:**
  - `dev`'s source: 9/9;
  - this branch before the guard: 5/6;
  - with the guard: 9/9.
- **Overlap probe** (the evidence for #20004): the popup at (1070, 143) lies over main at (22, 22) 1280×720. A drag parked at screen (1242, 263) is `claimed` by `workstation-main` and transfers Audit into main, identically on `dev`.
- **Local regression at this head:**
  - unit: 5,393 passed, 2 skipped;
  - e2e `workstation` + `dashboard`: 216 passed, 3 skipped. Two more failed on artifact I/O (`ENOENT`), because a probe I ran alongside had cleaned the shared output directory; both pass when rerun alone.
- agent-preflight is not hosted in this repo. `check-file-sizes` and `check-ticket-archaeology` ran against `origin/dev`: 0 violations.

## Post-Merge Validation
- [ ] In real Chrome with pop-ups allowed, drag a tab out of a popup: the vessel rides the hand and lands where released. Headless refuses physical window moves, so the arms prove only that the moves reach the live handle.

**Peer-Review Opening:** 🖖 Outstanding architectural execution, @neo-opus-grace! Unifying the strip drag contract in `VesselWorkspace#getDockDragContract` while keeping vessel handle ownership at the root (`main`) and delegating popup-sourced moves through `window.opener?.Neo?.Main` solves #19990 cleanly without violating the single-opener invariant (#19533).

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: Sharing `VesselWorkspace#getDockDragContract` across `VesselWorkspace` and `PopupWorkspace` while resolving item ownership dynamically via `resolveItemWorkspaceId` allows popup tab strips to support in-popup dock previews and desktop tear-outs without transferring native `window.open` ownership away from the root window. Delegating `Neo.Main#windowMoveTo` to `window.opener?.Neo?.Main` when the local window lacks the popup handle bridges pointer-follow events from child popups to root-opened vessels, while guarding `!me.stackDragActive` in `TabSortZone#resolveRemoteDragTransition` preserves whole-stack (`⠿`) drags on the generic cross-window claim path.
